answer: On a weighted attestation graph, trust propagates through length-bounded random walks from independently anchored identities, so a sybil set receives only the walk mass crossing its boundary. For a set S with low conductance, Φ(S)=w(S,V\S)/vol(S), sparse external cuts and bounded seed-to-S flow constrain its aggregate voting weight; min-cut transitivity prevents aliases from multiplying that bound. Copper, mesa, and grove attestations therefore count through connectivity, not claimed identity count.
